title: Perplexity
interviewAnswer: Perplexity is the exponential of average negative log-likelihood. Lower is better on the same data/tokenization, but perplexity is not directly comparable across different tokenizers.
why: Perplexity links sequence-model evaluation to information theory.
intuition: It loosely represents the model’s effective uncertainty over next-token choices.
deepDive: With natural logs, perplexity=exp(mean NLL). Tokenization changes sequence length and token probabilities, so cross-tokenizer comparisons can mislead.
followUps: Why can lower perplexity fail downstream?
production: Use task, safety, latency and cost metrics alongside perplexity.
workedExample: Two models using the same tokenizer can be compared on held-out perplexity; byte- and word-level perplexity should not be compared naively.
